messages:
Maya: Heads up — after today's rollout (merge: batch-scheduler-refactor) we see a clear perf regression in hosted canary. p99 generation latency +18-25% across models, KV cache miss rate jumped from ~2% -> ~11%. Canary was paused when alerts tripped. dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/2026-03-18/4872

Jon: saw the same in canary logs. Kicking off bisect now to isolate the offending commit. baseline vs head perf harness queued.

ci-bot: perf-ci: gen_latency_p99 increased by 22% (threshold 10%). Test run id: perf-2026-03-18-4872. See full report: https://ci.redwood.internal/perf/4872

Liam: quick profiler run on a repro vm shows kernel_selector spending more time than before. Flamegraph top functions: kernel_selector ~37%, continuous_batcher ~22%, kv_cache.lookup ~17%. Suspect extra memory copies in the scheduler reorder patch.

Alex: thanks. can you paste the flamegraph? Also try `git bisect` commands you used.

Liam: pasted flamegraph to thread (big 1.2MB svg). Bisect steps I ran:
```
git checkout v2026.03.17
git bisect start HEAD v2026.03.17
# run perf-harness --suite=gen_p99 --samples=200
# mark good/bad until commit abc1234..def5678
```
Bisect pointed at commit def5678: "scheduler: reorder batch types to prioritize streaming".

Sara: I reviewed def5678 — it introduced a new memcpy when shuffling request vectors to maintain ordering. That could explain extra CPU and worse cache locality for kernel selection. I opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3142 to revert the reorder in canary and added unit tests to prevent nondeterministic shuffles.

Jon: can we hold the full rollout and revert in prod? deploy-bot shows canary paused but full release still queued.

deploy-bot: Rollout status: canary paused, full rollout blocked by alert. Manual intervention required to continue.

Maya: agreed — hold and revert. Next steps: (1) revert def5678 in canary, (2) add a microbench for kernel_selector that exercises ordering code paths, (3) add a KV-cache regression test that asserts miss rate stays within 5% of baseline under synthetic workloads, (4) tune perf CI thresholds for p99 to be stricter (current 10% -> 7%) and add a flaky guard.

Alex: note: the memcpy happens only when batch ordering changes size classes. A more surgical fix may be to avoid memcpy when requests already in correct order. I'll draft a small patch to conditionally skip the shuffle. If that looks safe we can patch instead of full revert.

Liam: Sounds good. For the perf CI adjustments I recommend also adding a short synthetic workload that hits small sequence lengths (<64) — that's where we saw the biggest regression. I'll add it to perf-suite.

Sara: PR 3142 opened to revert + tests. I'll also add a deterministic seed for the batching shuffle in unit tests to prevent flakiness.

Maya: nice. Action log: bisect confirmed def5678; revert PR created; canary paused; perf CI threshold proposal posted to #eng-infra. Follow-ups: Alex & Liam to prototype conditional-skip patch, Sara to land revert and tests, infra to tighten thresholds and add microbench. We'll do a short post-release retro tomorrow and include test tightening in CI. :white_check_mark:

Jon: ordering owner here — if revert lands, let's run a focused perf sweep before resuming rollout. I can run the harness and share results in the thread.

ci-bot: reminder: create a ticket for flaky perf tests to track stabilization. Ticket created: PERF-721.

Maya: thanks all — keeping this thread pinned until rollout resumes.
